_comment: Every word the app shows, in one place. Edited here, compiled in - see cmake/UiStrings.cmake; CMake re-runs by itself when this file changes, and nothing extra ships next to the exe. Keys are dotted paths grouped by where the text appears, and become PascalCase identifiers with a k prefix (appearance.showItemBorders -> kAppearanceShowItemBorders). None of this text is an identifier the program depends on: every widget carries its own ##id, so any of it can be reworded freely. A key starting with an underscore is a note like this one and produces nothing.
_tools: The six tools: the name shown in the Shortcuts list, and the tooltips on the selection bar's drawing buttons.
tool.drawTip: Draw - drag on a snippet; hold Shift for a line, Ctrl for a rectangle
tool.eraseTip: Erase - drag over a snippet; hold Ctrl to erase a rectangle
bar.penTip: Pen - drag on the snippet to draw; right-click for a line or a rectangle
bar.lineTip: Line - drag from end to end; right-click for the other shapes
bar.rectangleTip: Rectangle - drag from corner to corner; right-click for the other shapes
bar.eraserTip: Eraser - drag over marks to erase them; right-click to erase a rectangle
bar.eraserRectTip: Rectangle eraser - drag over the region to erase; right-click for the round eraser
bar.colorTip: Color - choose the color to draw with, and how see-through it is
tool.textTip: Text - click the snippet to type into it
tool.selectTip: Select - click a snippet to select it, drag to move it, resize it by its handles (or right-drag it); double-click or hold on it to draw on it; Delete removes it
tool.newScreenshotTip: Screenshot - click for the whole screen or drag an area; then the tool you had is back
tool.newDrawingTip: New drawing - click for the whole screen or drag an area, then draw in it
_create: Actions that happen at once rather than being a tool.
_clipboard: What the clipboard does with the selected snippets - the four rows in the Shortcuts list, on Ctrl+C/X/V and Ctrl+D by default.
_popover: The popover a snippet's More button opens.
popover.backgroundFillTip: Opacity of the background fill color
popover.textSizeTip: Text size, in screen pixels - it doesn't scale when the item is resized
popover.keepAspectTip: Resizing by a handle keeps this snippet's shape - hold Shift for the other way
_menu: The context menus a right-click opens - on a snippet, on a canvas tile in the bar, and on empty canvas. Worded shorter than the popover's tooltips above: a menu row is read at a glance, next to its own icon and its own shortcut, not hovered for an explanation.
_deleted: What the Overview's Show deleted adds: deleted folders and canvases, marked out in red, each with Restore and Delete permanently.
deleted.restoreFolderTip: Restore the folder and every deleted canvas in it
deleted.restoreCanvasAndFolderTip: Restore the canvas, and its folder to hold it - the folder's other canvases stay deleted
deleted.deleteDeletedInFolderTip: Delete the deleted canvases in this folder permanently
deleted.goesOnUnknownDate: Deleted permanently on an unknown date
_itemChrome: The buttons on the bar that floats over the selected snippets.
item.pin: Pin - keep it on screen when the overlay is put away
_toasts: The brief messages that appear after something happened.
toast.copiedWithoutPicture: Copied without its picture - the original's could not be read
toast.purgedOne: 1 folder or canvas deleted over %d days ago was deleted permanently
toast.purgedMany: %zu folders and canvases deleted over %d days ago were deleted permanently
toast.notWritten: Not done - the library could not be written
toast.sentToDeletedCanvasPrefix: Undid paste - back on its deleted canvas, found under Show deleted:
_undoNames: What an undone or redone change is called, after the Undid/Redid prefix above.
_itemNames: The prefixes new snippets are named with, before their number.
_hotkeyText: How a key combination is written out wherever one is shown.
_hud: The input-options panel, whose rows the number keys toggle.
_tutorial: The tutorial's cards - see docs/TUTORIAL.md, section 4: each step's title and text, the lines under a text when a step needs something first (need.*) or sees a mistake coming (a step's miss*); the card's own words (card.*), and the card a skip ends on (skipped.*), the list of topics (list.* and topics.*), and its row in Settings > Interaction (settings.*). Step %d of %d takes the step and the count. Wrapped by the card, so written as running text. In braces, filled in as bound and set: {key:<command>} is the key that runs the command of that name (undo, cheatSheet, toggleEditMode, newScreenshotTool), {trigger:screenshot} and {trigger:drawing} the key held for a drag that makes one, {canvas} a canvas's name.
tutorial.welcome.title: Welcome to Spickzettel
tutorial.welcome.text:
Spickzettel keeps snippets - screenshots, drawings and notes - over whatever program is underneath, and everything saves itself.

A few steps show you the basics. They run in a folder of their own, so nothing you already have is touched.
tutorial.screenshot.title: Take a screenshot
tutorial.screenshot.text: Drag a box over anything on screen to take a screenshot of it.
tutorial.screenshot.textTrigger: Hold {trigger:screenshot} and drag a box over anything on screen to take a screenshot of it.
tutorial.screenshot.textTool: Press {key:newScreenshotTool}, then drag a box over anything on screen to take a screenshot of it.
tutorial.screenshot.textMenu: Right-click an empty spot and choose New screenshot, then drag a box over anything on screen to take a screenshot of it.
tutorial.screenshot.missFullscreen: That took the whole screen - a double-click does that. Press {key:deleteSelection} to delete it, and drag a box instead.
tutorial.screenshot.missDrawing: That made a drawing rather than a screenshot. Drag a box as above instead.
tutorial.move.title: Move it
tutorial.move.text: Drag it to move it. A press selects it, and a drag takes it along.
tutorial.move.missResized: That changed its size. Drag from the middle to move it.
tutorial.resize.title: Resize it
tutorial.resize.text: Drag a corner to resize it; Shift switches keeping its shape. A right-drag near an edge does it too.
tutorial.drawingMode.title: Draw on it
tutorial.drawingMode.text: Any snippet can be drawn on, a screenshot as well as a drawing. Double-click it, or hold the button down on it, to draw on it. The pen on its bar does the same once it is selected.
tutorial.draw.title: Draw
tutorial.color.title: Pick a color
tutorial.color.text: Press the color on the bar, and pick another. Click anywhere to close the chooser, then draw with it.
tutorial.color.missNothingDrawn: Give it a try and draw something.
tutorial.width.title: Change the width
tutorial.width.text: While you draw on a snippet, the wheel sets the pen's width. Turn it a few notches, then draw.
tutorial.width.missNothingDrawn: Give it a try and draw something.
tutorial.width.missOpacity: That changed its opacity. Turn the wheel without a key held.
tutorial.line.title: Draw a line
tutorial.line.text: Right-click the pen on the bar, or hold the button down on it, and choose Line: its icon turns into a line, and a drag draws a straight one. Holding Shift does the same for one stroke.
tutorial.line.missFreehand: That was the pen. Right-click it on the bar and choose Line.
tutorial.rectangle.title: Draw a rectangle
tutorial.rectangle.text: The same menu has Rectangle: choose it, and drag one. Holding Ctrl does the same for one stroke. Pen, in the menu, brings the pen back.
tutorial.rectangle.missLine: That was a line. Right-click the pen on the bar and choose Rectangle.
tutorial.erase.title: Erase
tutorial.erase.text: Press the eraser on the bar, and drag over what you drew. It cuts through strokes.
tutorial.eraseRect.title: Erase a rectangle
tutorial.eraseRect.text: Right-click the eraser, or hold the button down on it, and choose Rectangle eraser. Drag one across what's left. Holding Ctrl does the same for one drag.
tutorial.eraseRect.missRound: That was the round eraser. Right-click it on the bar and choose Rectangle eraser.
tutorial.eraseRight.title: Erase with the right button
tutorial.eraseRight.text: The right button erases with any tool. Press the pen, then hold the right button and drag across what's left.
tutorial.eraseRight.missEraser: That was the eraser. Press the pen, then drag with the right button.
tutorial.note.title: Write a note
tutorial.note.text: Press Text on the bar, click the snippet, and type a note.
tutorial.note.missTyping: Press Esc or click outside it when you're done.
tutorial.stopDrawing.title: Stop drawing
tutorial.stopDrawing.text: Click outside it, or press Esc, to stop drawing. The tool lit on the bar, pressed again, does it too.
tutorial.delete.title: Delete it
tutorial.delete.text: Select it and press Delete, or the close button on its bar.
tutorial.undo.title: Bring it back
tutorial.undo.text: Deleted by mistake? {key:undo} brings it back. It takes back anything you did, a step at a time.
tutorial.programs.title: Set it up for your programs
tutorial.programs.text: Some games break when the overlay takes focus; others need it to. Look through Settings > Behavior, and make a profile for each program that needs its own.
tutorial.antiCheat.title: Careful with anti-cheat
tutorial.antiCheat.text: Some games watch for tools that draw over them or read their input. If a game might object, quit Spickzettel before you start it.
tutorial.away.title: Back to your program
tutorial.away.text: Press {key:toggleEditMode} to put the overlay away and go back to your program. Press it again to come back here.
tutorial.away.textTray: Click the Spickzettel icon in the notification area to put the overlay away and go back to your program. Click it again to come back here.
tutorial.end.title: That's the basics
tutorial.end.text:
{key:cheatSheet} shows every key and gesture, and a right-click on anything shows what it can do.

More topics has the others, and this one again. The tutorial is also in Settings > Interaction.
tutorial.end.textNoCheatSheetKey:
Right-click an empty spot for the cheat sheet, with every key and gesture; a right-click on anything shows what it can do.

More topics has the others, and this one again. The tutorial is also in Settings > Interaction.
tutorial.drawingEnd.title: That's drawing and notes
tutorial.drawingEnd.text: Double-click any snippet, or press the pen on its bar, to draw on it. Clear drawing, in its right-click menu, takes every stroke away; More, on its bar, has the note's color and size.
tutorial.pin.title: Pin it
tutorial.pin.text: A pinned snippet stays on screen when you put the overlay away, so it can sit over your game while you play. Select it, and press Pin on the bar above it.
tutorial.pinnedAway.title: Put the overlay away
tutorial.pinnedAway.text:
Press {key:toggleEditMode} to put the overlay away. The pinned snippet stays over your program, and your clicks go through to it.

Press {key:toggleEditMode} again to come back here.
tutorial.pinnedAway.textTray:
Click the Spickzettel icon in the notification area to put the overlay away. The pinned snippet stays over your program, and your clicks go through to it.

Click the icon again to come back here.
tutorial.pinnedAway.missViewMode: That was view mode, which keeps everything on screen - it comes next. Put the overlay away as above, and only the pinned snippet stays.
tutorial.opacity.title: Make it see-through
tutorial.opacity.text:
Make it see-through, so it hides less of what's underneath: hold Ctrl and turn the wheel.

Shift and the wheel fade what's drawn on it instead, and the wheel alone resizes it. More, on its bar, has the same as sliders.
tutorial.opacity.missResized: That changed its size. Hold Ctrl as you turn the wheel.
tutorial.opacity.missNothingDrawn: Shift fades what's drawn on it, and nothing is yet. Hold Ctrl instead.
tutorial.viewMode.title: View mode
tutorial.viewMode.text:
View mode keeps everything on this canvas on screen, pinned or not, and your clicks go through to your program.

Press {key:toggleViewMode} to switch to it, and {key:toggleEditMode} to come back here.
tutorial.viewMode.textTray:
View mode keeps everything on this canvas on screen, pinned or not, and your clicks go through to your program.

Press {key:toggleViewMode} to switch to it, and click the Spickzettel icon in the notification area to come back here.
tutorial.viewMode.textNoKey:
View mode keeps everything on this canvas on screen, pinned or not, and your clicks go through to your program.

It has no key yet. Set one in Settings > Hotkeys to use it, and go on with Next.
tutorial.viewMode.missAway: That put the overlay away, and only what's pinned stayed. Press {key:toggleViewMode} for view mode.
tutorial.unpin.title: Unpin it
tutorial.unpin.text: A pinned snippet stays on screen until you unpin it, even after the tutorial. Press Pin on its bar again.
tutorial.pinningEnd.title: That's pinning and view mode
tutorial.pinningEnd.text:
Pin what you need while you play, and make it see-through so it doesn't hide the game. View mode keeps the whole canvas in sight.

The bar's Fullscreen fills the screen with a snippet, and its More has the opacity, the background color and the text.
tutorial.newDrawing.title: Make a drawing
tutorial.newDrawing.text: A drawing is a blank snippet to draw or write on. Drag a box on an empty spot to make one.
tutorial.newDrawing.textTrigger: A drawing is a blank snippet to draw or write on. Hold {trigger:drawing} and drag a box on an empty spot to make one.
tutorial.newDrawing.textTool: A drawing is a blank snippet to draw or write on. Press {key:newDrawingTool}, then drag a box on an empty spot to make one.
tutorial.newDrawing.textMenu: A drawing is a blank snippet to draw or write on. Right-click an empty spot and choose New drawing, then drag a box to make one.
tutorial.newDrawing.missFullscreen: That took the whole screen - a double-click does that. Press {key:deleteSelection} to delete it, and drag a box instead.
tutorial.newDrawing.missScreenshot: That made a screenshot rather than a drawing. Make one as above.
tutorial.fullscreen.title: Screenshot the whole screen
tutorial.fullscreen.text: Double-click an empty spot, or hold the button down on it, to take a screenshot of the whole screen.
tutorial.fullscreen.textTrigger: Hold {trigger:screenshot} and double-click an empty spot, or hold the button down on it, to take a screenshot of the whole screen.
tutorial.fullscreen.textTool: Press {key:newScreenshotTool}, then click anywhere to take a screenshot of the whole screen.
tutorial.fullscreen.textMenu: Right-click an empty spot and choose Fullscreen screenshot to take a screenshot of the whole screen.
tutorial.fullscreen.missDrawingMode: That made a drawing of the whole screen. Press Esc to stop drawing on it.
tutorial.fullscreen.missDelete: That made a drawing of the whole screen. Press {key:deleteSelection} to delete it, and take a screenshot as above.
tutorial.fullscreen.missBox: That took a part of the screen. Double-click instead of dragging.
tutorial.fullscreen.missDrawing: That made a drawing rather than a screenshot. Take one as above.
tutorial.quickCapture.title: Capture from your program
tutorial.quickCapture.text:
The capture hotkeys work while the overlay is away, so you can grab your game without opening the overlay first.

Press {key:toggleEditMode} to put the overlay away, then press {key:quickCapture}. It takes a screenshot of the whole screen and brings the overlay back with it, on a new canvas of its own.
tutorial.quickCapture.textTray:
The capture hotkeys work while the overlay is away, so you can grab your game without opening the overlay first.

Click the Spickzettel icon in the notification area to put the overlay away, then press {key:quickCapture}. It takes a screenshot of the whole screen and brings the overlay back with it, on a new canvas of its own.
tutorial.quickCapture.textNoKey:
The quick capture takes a screenshot of the whole screen from any program, and brings the overlay up with it, on a new canvas of its own.

It has no working key yet. Set one in Settings > Hotkeys to use it, and go on with Next.
tutorial.quickCapture.missSilent: That was the background capture, which comes next. Press {key:quickCapture} for this one.
tutorial.silentCapture.title: Capture in the background
tutorial.silentCapture.text:
{key:silentCapture} captures the same way, but the overlay stays away, so your game keeps the focus.

Put the overlay away, press {key:silentCapture}, then press {key:toggleEditMode} to come back and see the capture.
tutorial.silentCapture.textTray:
{key:silentCapture} captures the same way, but the overlay stays away, so your game keeps the focus.

Click the Spickzettel icon in the notification area to put the overlay away, press {key:silentCapture}, then click the icon again to come back and see the capture.
tutorial.silentCapture.textNoKey:
The background capture takes the same screenshot, but the overlay stays away, so your game keeps the focus.

It has no working key yet. Set one in Settings > Hotkeys to use it, and go on with Next.
tutorial.silentCapture.missQuick: That was the quick capture, which brings the overlay up. Put it away, and press {key:silentCapture} instead.
tutorial.capturingEnd.title: That's capturing
tutorial.newCanvas.title: A new canvas
tutorial.newCanvas.text: A folder holds canvases, and each canvas its own snippets. Move the pointer to the bottom edge of the screen: the canvas bar comes out with this folder's canvases. Press + on it for a new canvas.
tutorial.newCanvas.textKey: A folder holds canvases, and each canvas its own snippets. Press {key:newCanvas} for a new canvas.
tutorial.newCanvas.textOverview: A folder holds canvases, and each canvas its own snippets. Right-click an empty spot, choose Overview, and press New canvas at the bottom.
tutorial.moveSnippet.title: Take a snippet along
tutorial.moveSnippet.text: To take a snippet to another canvas, select it and press {key:cut}. Go to the other canvas - hold Alt and turn the wheel, or click its tile on the canvas bar - and press {key:paste} there.
tutorial.moveSnippet.textNoBar: To take a snippet to another canvas, select it and press {key:cut}. Go to the other canvas - hold Alt and turn the wheel - and press {key:paste} there.
tutorial.moveSnippet.textMenu: To take a snippet to another canvas, right-click it and choose Cut. Go to the other canvas - hold Alt and turn the wheel, or click its tile on the canvas bar - then right-click an empty spot and choose Paste.
tutorial.moveSnippet.textMenuNoBar: To take a snippet to another canvas, right-click it and choose Cut. Go to the other canvas - hold Alt and turn the wheel - then right-click an empty spot and choose Paste.
tutorial.moveSnippet.missCopy: That pasted a copy - the first one is still on the other canvas. Cut it to move it instead.
tutorial.overview.title: The Overview
tutorial.overview.text: The Overview has all your folders and canvases. Open it with the grid button at the right end of the canvas bar.
tutorial.overview.textMenu: The Overview has all your folders and canvases. Right-click an empty spot and choose Overview to open it.
tutorial.newFolder.title: A new folder
tutorial.newFolder.text: Folders keep canvases apart - one for each game, say. Press New folder, at the bottom left. It comes with a canvas, and takes you there.
tutorial.newFolder.missCanvas: That made a canvas. New folder is the button to its left.
tutorial.rename.title: A name
tutorial.rename.text: It's named for the time it was made. Double-click the name, type a better one, and press Enter. A canvas is renamed the same way, by the name under its tile.
tutorial.switchFolder.title: Back to the tutorial
tutorial.switchFolder.text: A folder's row shows its canvases, and a tile takes you there. Click the tutorial's folder in the list, then one of its canvases.
tutorial.moveCanvas.title: Sort a canvas
tutorial.moveCanvas.text: To move a canvas to another folder, drag its tile onto the folder in the list. Drag one of these onto your folder.
tutorial.deleteCanvas.title: Delete a canvas
tutorial.deleteCanvas.text: The trash button under a tile deletes that canvas, with its snippets. Delete the one your snippet is on.
tutorial.showDeleted.title: The trash
tutorial.showDeleted.text: Nothing deleted is gone yet. Tick Show deleted, at the top right: what's in the trash shows in red, where it was.
tutorial.restore.title: Restore
tutorial.restore.text: Press Restore, the arrow under its tile: the canvas comes back, with its snippet.
tutorial.foldersEnd.title: That's folders and canvases
tutorial.foldersEnd.text: A snippet's right-click menu has two more ways to move it: Move to canvas, which picks one in the Overview, and Move to new canvas. A right-click on a tile of the canvas bar deletes that canvas.
tutorial.capturingEnd.text: Each capture is on a canvas of its own, so they're easy to tell apart: the Overview, in the right-click menu, shows them side by side. A right-click on an empty spot also lists every way to make a snippet, with the keys beside them.
tutorial.openProfiles.title: Profiles
tutorial.openProfiles.text: Programs differ: some games break when the overlay takes focus, others need it to. A profile keeps settings for one program. Right-click an empty spot, choose Settings, and pick Profiles on the left.
tutorial.openProfiles.textOverview: Programs differ: some games break when the overlay takes focus, others need it to. A profile keeps settings for one program. Press Settings, at the top of the Overview, and pick Profiles on the left.
tutorial.makeProfile.title: A profile for this program
tutorial.makeProfile.text: The overlay is up over {underneath}. Press Make a profile for this: it runs whenever the overlay comes up over {underneath}, and says "currently active" while it does.
tutorial.makeProfile.missBlank: That made a blank profile, which matches no program until you name one. Make a profile for this is the button to its left.
tutorial.makeProfile.missTaken: {running} is already the profile for {underneath}, and the first in the list that matches is the one that runs. Make another anyway, for practice: it won't run, but the steps work the same.
tutorial.behavior.title: What it can change
tutorial.behavior.text: A profile can change what is in the boxes marked Per profile: the settings in Behavior, and the shortcuts in Hotkeys. Pick Behavior on the left.
tutorial.change.title: Change a setting
tutorial.change.text: Profile, at the top of the box, says whose settings are below: {profile}'s. Untick Don't steal focus. Over {program}, the overlay will now take focus, and the rows under it gray out: they only matter while it doesn't. Over any other program the defaults apply, and Profile shows them.
tutorial.revert.title: Back to the default
tutorial.revert.text: To hand a setting back to the defaults, press the arrow beside it. Ticking it again would keep it {profile}'s own, in the accent color.
tutorial.revert.missTickedBack: That keeps it {profile}'s own - the row is still in the accent color. The arrow beside it hands it back to the defaults.
tutorial.profilesEnd.title: That's profiles
tutorial.profilesEnd.text: New empty profile makes one for a program that isn't in front. Open a profile's row to add more programs to it, or part of a window's title. The first profile in the list that matches is the one that runs.
tutorial.need.inTutorialFolder: The tutorial is in a folder of its own.
tutorial.need.closeOverview: Close the Overview to go on.
tutorial.need.closeCheatSheet: Close the cheat sheet to go on.
tutorial.need.closePopup: Press Esc to close what is open, and go on.
tutorial.need.noDrawingMode: Click outside the snippet, or press Esc, to stop drawing first.
tutorial.need.noOtherTool: Press Esc to put the tool down first.
tutorial.need.aSubject: Take a screenshot to practice on, or let me put one here.
tutorial.need.subjectOnScreen: It went to the dock. Click it there to bring it back.
tutorial.need.subjectCanMove: It fills the screen. Right-click it and choose Fullscreen to shrink it back.
tutorial.need.drawingOnSubject: Double-click it to draw on it again.
tutorial.need.deletedSubject: Delete it again to try this, or go on with Next.
tutorial.need.subjectPinned: It isn't pinned. Select it, and press Pin on its bar.
tutorial.need.penInHand: Press the pen on the bar.
tutorial.need.subjectDrawnOn: Nothing is drawn on it to erase. Draw something with the pen first.
tutorial.need.overviewUp: Open the Overview: right-click an empty spot and choose Overview.
tutorial.need.canvasesTab: Go back to the Canvases tab, at the top left.
tutorial.need.deletedShown: Tick Show deleted, at the top right, to see it.
tutorial.need.somethingInTrash: Nothing of the tutorial's is in the trash. Delete a canvas first, or go on with Next.
tutorial.need.settingsUp: Open Settings: right-click an empty spot and choose Settings.
tutorial.need.settingsTab: Press Settings, at the top of the Overview.
tutorial.need.profilesSection: Pick Profiles in the list on the left.
tutorial.need.behaviorSection: Pick Behavior in the list on the left.
tutorial.need.aProgramUnderneath: The overlay is up over nothing it can name. Press {key:toggleEditMode} to put it away, click the program you want a profile for, and press it again.
tutorial.need.aProgramUnderneathTray: The overlay is up over nothing it can name. Click the Spickzettel icon in the notification area to put it away, click the program you want a profile for, and click the icon again.
tutorial.need.tutorialsProfile: The tutorial has no profile of its own: it was deleted, or the app has restarted since. Go Back to make one, or go on with Next.
tutorial.need.showingIt: Profile is on {showing}. Pick {profile} there: a change is made to whose settings it shows.
tutorial.need.somethingSetInIt: {profile} sets nothing of its own yet. Untick Don't steal focus in it first, or go on with Next.
tutorial.card.nextWaits: The next steps use what this one makes.
tutorial.skipped.title: Tutorial skipped
tutorial.skipped.again: More topics has this one again, and the others. The tutorial is also in Settings > Interaction.
tutorial.list.title: Tutorial
tutorial.list.text: Pick a topic. Each runs from its first step, most in a new folder of their own.
tutorial.settings.heading: Tutorial
tutorial.settings.help:
The tutorial shows you around, one topic at a time: the basics, pinning and view mode, drawing and notes, capturing, folders and canvases, and profiles. Take any topic again whenever you want a refresher.

Most topics run in a new folder of their own, away from your canvases. A folder from an earlier run is left as it is.
tutorial.topics.basics.title: Basics
tutorial.topics.basics.gist: Take a screenshot, move and resize it, delete it and bring it back, and go back to your program.
tutorial.topics.pinning.title: Pinning and view mode
tutorial.topics.pinning.gist: Keep a snippet on screen over your program, make it see-through, and let your clicks through.
tutorial.topics.drawing.title: Drawing and notes
tutorial.topics.drawing.gist: Draw on a snippet: the color, the width, shapes, the eraser, and a note.
tutorial.topics.capturing.title: Capturing
tutorial.topics.capturing.gist: Make a drawing, screenshot the whole screen, and capture from your program with a hotkey.
tutorial.topics.folders.title: Folders and canvases
tutorial.topics.folders.gist: Make and switch canvases, move a snippet, sort canvases into folders, and restore from the trash.
tutorial.topics.profiles.title: Profiles
tutorial.topics.profiles.gist: Make a profile for a program, change a setting in it, and hand it back to the defaults.
_cheatSheet: The cheat sheet (Ctrl+H by default): every key and gesture, in groups. Each row is what you press, then what it does; a shortcut that is unbound drops its row. After a modifier, a gesture is capitalized like a key (Ctrl+Drag), so the left column reads as one kind of thing.
cheatSheet.title: Cheat sheet
cheatSheet.quickCapture: Capture the screen to a new canvas
cheatSheet.esc: Put the tool down, stop drawing, deselect
cheatSheet.rightClick: A menu for whatever is under the pointer
cheatSheet.screenshotTool: Screenshot: click for all, or drag
cheatSheet.drawingTool: Drawing: click for all, or drag
cheatSheet.box: Select with a box, from empty canvas
cheatSheet.resize: Resize; Shift toggles keeping the shape
cheatSheet.nudge: Nudge a pixel; with Shift, ten
cheatSheet.altWheel: Previous, next canvas in the folder
cheatSheet.bottomEdge: The canvas bar; drag a canvas to reorder
cheatSheet.dragTile: Reorder, or drop it on a folder
_demo: The watermark a demo build carries. Only ever drawn by that build.
demo.title: Spickzettel
demo.subtitle: Demo Version
_status: The warning along the bottom while the disk cannot be written to - see OverlayApp::RenderPersistenceWarning. %s is a path.
status.writeFailed: Could not write to the library at %s, so the last change was not made - it is back as it was
status.configWriteFailed: Could not write the settings to %s
_startup: The message boxes shown when the app cannot start at all, before there is a tray icon to say so.
startup.failed: Spickzettel could not start. Another copy may already be running.
startup.configSetAside:
Spickzettel could not read its settings file, %s, and started with the default settings.

The file was kept beside it as %s, so nothing in it is lost. Deleting deleted folders and canvases permanently is switched off until it is switched on again in Settings > Behavior.
startup.configUnreadable:
Spickzettel could not read its settings file, %s, and started with the default settings.

The file was left as it is, and settings changed until the next start will not be saved. Nothing deleted was erased for good at this start.
startup.configNewer: Spickzettel's settings file, %s, was saved by a newer version of Spickzettel. This version started with what it could read from it and leaves the file as it is, so settings changed until the next start will not be saved. Nothing deleted was erased for good at this start.
startup.librarySetAside:
Spickzettel could not read its library file, %s - it is not a library this version can open, or it is damaged - and started with an empty library.

The file was kept beside it as %s, so nothing in it is lost.
startup.hotkeysTaken:
Spickzettel started, but these hotkeys are already used by another application and do nothing:
%s

The tray icon's menu opens the overlay without them, and Settings > Hotkeys can give them other keys.
startup.newerLibrary: Spickzettel could not start: your library was saved by a newer version of Spickzettel. This version would lose what the newer one saved, so it leaves the library alone. Please use the newer version.
startup.libraryUnreadable: Spickzettel could not start: it could not read its library file, %s. Nothing was changed. Another program may be holding it - a backup or sync tool, say - or the file's permissions may not let Spickzettel read it. Start Spickzettel again once the file can be read.
_prerelease: The notice a prerelease build shows at every start (see build::kPrereleaseNotice). %s is the version line.
prerelease.title: Spickzettel - Prerelease
prerelease.body:
This is a prerelease build of Spickzettel, version %s.

It is for testing only. Please do not redistribute it or pass it on to anyone else.
_tray: The system tray icon's own menu.
_placeholders: Some strings below carry printf placeholders - %s for a word, %zu for a count, %d%% for a percentage. Keep every one of them, and in the same order: they are filled in at runtime, and a missing or extra one is a crash rather than a typo.
_formats: How a number reads where one is shown - the unit, and the spacing before it.
_overview: The panel the canvas bar's Overview button opens: three tabs across the top, and the canvas grid under the first.
overview.showDeletedHelp: Show deleted folders and canvases where they were, in red, to restore or delete permanently
overview.previewsVectorHelp: Draw each snippet's vector strokes in the canvas thumbnails
overview.previewsBitmapHelp: Draw screenshots too. Their pixels aren't in memory for canvases you aren't on, so each one is read and scaled down while this panel is open - and released again when it closes.
overview.folderEmpty: This folder has no canvases yet.
overview.libraryEmpty: No canvases anywhere yet - "New canvas" makes one.
_moveCopy: The picker an item's "Move to another canvas" opens, and the button that confirms it.
_deleteConfirm: The confirmation before a canvas or folder is deleted, and before anything already deleted is deleted for good.
deleteConfirm.promptDeletedIn: Delete the deleted canvases in "%s" permanently?
deleteConfirm.alsoCanvases: This also deletes every canvas inside it.
deleteConfirm.alsoCanvasesMany: This also deletes every canvas inside them.
deleteConfirm.restorable: It can be restored with "Show deleted" in the Overview.
deleteConfirm.restorableFor: It can be restored with "Show deleted" in the Overview for %d days. After that it is deleted permanently.
deleteConfirm.restorableMany: They can be restored with "Show deleted" in the Overview.
deleteConfirm.restorableForMany: They can be restored with "Show deleted" in the Overview for %d days. After that they are deleted permanently.
_settingsTabs: The list down the left of the Settings tab.
settings.scopeProfileNote: Settings that can be overridden per profile
settings.notSavedNewer: Changes made here apply until Spickzettel exits, and are not saved: the settings file, %s, was saved by a newer version of Spickzettel and is left as it is.
settings.notSavedUnreadable: Changes made here apply until Spickzettel exits, and are not saved: the settings file, %s, could not be read and is left as it is.
_defaults: Settings > Defaults: what a new snippet starts with.
defaults.screenshotHelp:
What a screenshot starts with when it is made.

Each of these is the snippet's own from then on, changed in its popover (the More button on its bar). Changing one here leaves every snippet already made as it is.
defaults.drawingHelp:
What a drawing starts with when it is made.

A drawing starts see-through. Raise its background opacity to give every new one a backing, in the color below.

Each of these is the snippet's own from then on, changed in its popover (the More button on its bar). Changing one here leaves every snippet already made as it is.
defaults.textHelp:
The size and color text starts with in a new snippet.

The size is in screen pixels, and does not change when the snippet is resized. It starts at 20, times the display scale Windows had when Spickzettel first ran.

The color's alpha is the text's opacity.
defaults.keepAspectHelp:
Resizing by a handle keeps the snippet's shape. Hold Shift while dragging for the other way.

A snippet's own popover can change this for that snippet alone.
appearance.monitorHelp:
Which monitor the overlay comes up on.

"Primary display" is whichever monitor Windows treats as the main one. Pick a monitor by name and the overlay stays with that monitor. While it isn't connected the overlay uses the primary display, and it goes back as soon as the monitor returns.

A change applies at once, with the overlay moving to the monitor you picked.
appearance.uiScaleHelp:
How large the overlay's own text, buttons and panels are drawn.

"Match Windows" uses the scale Windows is set to for the monitor the overlay is on (Settings > System > Display > Scale), and follows it when that changes. Pick a size to use that one instead, whatever Windows is set to.

Snippets, drawings and the text in notes keep their own sizes: they are what is on your screen, not the interface to it.
appearance.accentHelp:
The color of whatever is selected, active or current: tabs, the tool in hand, checkboxes and sliders, the current canvas. Text and icons drawn on it switch between dark and light to stay readable.

The border of a pinned snippet has a color of its own, under Snippet colors.
appearance.showItemBordersHelp:
Every snippet gets a border, not just the one in front - handy for spotting a still-empty Drawing item.

The frontmost snippet keeps its own border either way: that border is what says it is in front.
appearance.imageFilterHelp:
How screenshots are drawn at a size other than their own.

Bilinear: what the graphics card does by default. Soft when enlarged; below about half size, thin lines and text break up.

Nearest: whole pixels, unblended. Blocky when enlarged, which suits pixel art and small captures blown up.

Bicubic: sharper than bilinear when enlarged, and clean when shrunk.

Lanczos: the sharpest, at a little more cost. Hard edges can show a faint halo.

Takes effect immediately; the pictures themselves are not changed.
appearance.snippetColorsHelp:
Which snippet is on top, in color: the frontmost one is drawn in its own border color, everything behind it in the other.

Alpha is part of each color - a border you can see more of the screen through is how you make the snippets behind recede.

Hovering is shown separately, as a thicker border, so it never reads as "this one is in front". A selected snippet's border is drawn in the accent color instead.

A pinned snippet's border is always drawn, in its own color: those are the snippets that stay on screen when the overlay is put away.
appearance.showEditBorder: Show a border around the screen while edit mode is active
appearance.showEditBorderHelp:
A frame around the whole screen for as long as the overlay is up in edit mode, so it's obvious your clicks are landing here rather than in whatever's underneath.

View-only mode never draws it - input passes straight through there, so there's nothing to warn about.
appearance.editBorderEmptyOnly: Show border only while the canvas is still empty
appearance.editBorderEmptyOnlyHelp: The border disappears as soon as there's anything on the current canvas - by then that content is itself the proof the overlay is up, and the frame has nothing left to say.
appearance.showCanvasBar: Show the canvas bar at the bottom of the screen
appearance.showCanvasBarHelp: A bar along the bottom edge with the canvases of the folder you are in, to switch between them or start a new one. It keeps out of the way: it slides out when the pointer reaches the bottom of the screen, and for a moment whenever the canvas changes or the overlay comes up.
_drawing: Settings > Interaction: the Snippets section at its top.
_bars: Settings > Interaction: the bar that floats over the selection, and the buttons its two groups carry.
bars.heading: Toolbar above a snippet
bars.help:
The small bar that floats over what you have selected: the drawing tools, and what can be done to the snippet. A drawing tool pressed there starts drawing on the snippet; pressed again, it stops.

Click a button to show or hide it. Drag one onto another to move it there. Hidden buttons stay in the row, dimmed, so switching one back on puts it where it was.
bars.resetTip: Put this row back the way it ships: every button, in its original order
drawing.raiseSelected: Bring a snippet to the front when selecting it
drawing.raiseSelectedHelp:
On: clicking a snippet, or taking hold of it to drag it, puts it in front of the others - the way a window manager raises a window you click. Taking hold of one of several selected snippets brings all of them forward, in the order they already have; Shift-clicking to add to the selection changes no order.

Off: selecting leaves the order alone, as in a drawing program; the order is changed from a snippet's context menu (right-click it).
creation.heading: Making a snippet on an empty spot
creation.help:
What a press of the left button on empty space makes: dragged, a snippet of the size dragged; double-clicked or held still, a fullscreen one. A plain click makes nothing.

Each kind can have its own press - a plain one, or one with Ctrl or Alt held - or none, and is then made from the menu a right-click on empty space opens, or with its key. Choosing the press the other kind has swaps the two.

Shift is not among them: Shift-drag on empty space draws a box that selects.
settings.confirmDeleteHelp:
Asks before a folder or canvas is deleted. It can still be restored afterwards, with Show deleted in the Overview.

Off: it is deleted on the press, the way a snippet is.
settings.confirmDeleteForGoodHelp:
Asks before a folder or canvas that is already deleted is deleted permanently, with Show deleted in the Overview. That cannot be undone.

Off: it is deleted permanently on the press.
settings.purgeDeletedHelp:
Off: a deleted folder or canvas stays deleted until you restore it or delete it permanently, both with Show deleted in the Overview.

On: once it has been deleted for longer than this, it is deleted permanently the next time Spickzettel starts. A canvas deleted along with its folder goes with the folder.

Deleted snippets are never kept past a restart: undo brings them back, and nothing else does.
debug.heading: What to draw on top
debug.showDebugOverlayHelp: Border around the screen plus a status line (stroke count, mouse position) - confirms the overlay is receiving input at all.
debug.showFrameGraphHelp: A graph of the last ten seconds, top right: how long each frame took to come, and under it when the library was written or flushed to the disk, a picture encoded or read, the screen captured or the settings saved - for telling what a stutter was.
debug.showInputHudHelp:
Lists every option from the Behavior section with its current state, plus a frame rate, and flips each one with a number key - for finding the combination that works while standing in front of the game rather than in here.

While it's up, the number keys 1-6 belong to the overlay and don't reach the game, even with 'Don't forward keystrokes' off - though only while 'Don't steal focus' is on, since otherwise the overlay has the keyboard anyway.
_about: The About tab: what this build is, who owns it, and what else is inside it.
about.copyright: (c) 2026 The Spickzettel Authors. All rights reserved.
_aboutComponents: The Built with list. Names as their own projects spell them, so they can be looked up.
_input: Settings > Behavior - what the overlay does to the application underneath.
input.underneathHelp: The application the overlay is currently up over. Every setting in this section is an answer to a question about that application, and this is the identity a profile is matched on - so it is worth being able to see it, including seeing it come up empty.
input.nothingIdentifiable: Nothing identifiable - no window in front, or one that won't say what it is.
input.unreadableExecutableHelp: Its image path can't be read from here. That means a program belonging to another account, or a game shielded by anti-cheat - not simply one running as administrator, which answers like any other. Match it on its window title instead.
input.editModeHelp:
What edit mode does to the application underneath while you draw on top of it. All on by default; which combination works still depends on the game, so they stay separately switchable.

A row sits under the row it needs, and is grayed out for as long as that one is off - keeping its own setting until then, which is why it shows a dash rather than a check mark: stored, but not doing anything.
input.dontStealFocusHelp:
Edit mode stays mouse-only and leaves keyboard focus with whatever's underneath (e.g. a game), so it won't pause or throttle just from the overlay being shown.

That also leaves the game receiving input, since most games gate camera-look on being the foreground window rather than on being covered - which is what everything nested under this row is for. Turn this off and those options have nothing left to do.
input.dontForwardKeystrokesHelp:
Typing near the overlay stops reaching the game entirely, so no more walking forward while naming a canvas. The hotkeys keep working, including the one that turns edit mode off again. Windows' own shortcuts - the Windows key, Alt+Tab - wait until edit mode is off. A text field that needs real typing borrows the keyboard back for as long as it's open.

With edit mode taking focus instead, the game already receives no keystrokes and there is nothing here to take.
input.rawMouseHelp:
Take the mouse from the game: clicks and drags over the overlay stop reaching it, and the pointer is driven from the mouse's own movement counts instead of from the Windows cursor. That is what makes the overlay usable over a game that hides the pointer, pins it, or snaps it back to the middle of the screen.

It does not stop the game looking around. First-person games read mouse movement by a route nothing outside the game can intercept, so expect the camera to keep turning while you draw - which is what countering, below, tries to do something about.
input.takeFocusOverElevatedHelp:
Windows hands an application running with higher privileges than the overlay - anything started as administrator - none of its input to anything below it. On an account with administrator rights that includes Task Manager, which asks for the highest privileges it can have; on an account without them it runs at the same level as everything else and nothing here applies. Over one of those the overlay gets no pointer movement and none of its own shortcuts, whatever the options below say. Taking focus is the only thing that brings either back, so edit mode does that for as long as such an application is in front.

Only when it can tell. A program that refuses to answer the question is left alone, because a game behind anti-cheat refuses it in exactly the same way, and taking focus from a game is what the row above exists to prevent.

Turn it off to keep hands off regardless, and accept an overlay you cannot draw on or type into there. Pinned snippets still show and the capture hotkeys still work.
input.counterRawMouseHelp:
Keeps count of every movement the game reads and feeds it the exact opposite, so a camera integrating raw motion ends up where it started. The opposite is fed in steps - whenever the camera has strayed past the threshold below, and once more as you leave edit mode - so in between the camera wanders. Pairs with freezing the screen, which hides that.

Needs the mouse to have been taken first, and not for plumbing reasons: a correction travels to the game as ordinary mouse movement, through the same arithmetic Windows uses to move its cursor, so with Windows still driving that cursor the correction cancels your own slow movement as well. Measured: 22 pixels of slow travel became 1.

Expect nothing at all from games that ignore synthetic input, which includes anything with anti-cheat.
input.counterThresholdHelp:
How far the camera may stray, in mouse counts on either axis, before it is set back. A camera stops at straight up and straight down, and a correction made after it stopped overshoots by what it could not follow - so the game ends up looking somewhere else.

If that happens, lower this; the higher your in-game sensitivity, the lower it needs to be. Lower means more corrections, each one a moment the camera jumps - behind a frozen screen, not something you see. Best set per game, in its profile.
input.softwarePointerHelp:
Which pointer you see while the mouse is taken - not where it is. The overlay keeps the position either way, to sub-pixel precision, from the mouse's own movement counts.

On, it is drawn into the overlay's own frame. Off, that same position is written to the ordinary Windows cursor, which costs nothing to draw and moves at the mouse's report rate rather than at the frame rate - noticeably better over a VM console or a remote desktop, where a drawn pointer has to travel as pixels.

Off can't win against a game that holds the cursor for mouse-look: it puts the cursor back in the middle of the screen every frame, and no other process can see or out-vote that. Against those, the drawn pointer is the one that stays where you put it.

With nothing taken from the game, this is purely cosmetic - Windows is moving the pointer and this only changes how it looks.
input.freezeScreenHelp:
On entering edit mode, grab what is on screen and draw on that instead of on the live application. The game carries on underneath - it just isn't shown, so a camera that drifts or twitches while you draw stops being something you have to watch.

The picture is taken fresh on each entry into edit mode and dropped when you leave, so switching this on takes effect the next time you open the overlay. A game in exclusive fullscreen may refuse to be captured; if the screen comes up blank rather than frozen, switch that game to borderless windowed.

A screenshot snippet taken while the screen is frozen is cut out of the frozen picture, so what you drag out is what you were looking at.
_hotkeys: Settings > Hotkeys, and the Shortcuts rows below them.
hotkeys.summoningHelp:
The keys that reach the overlay from anywhere, whatever has focus - three that bring it up, and one that deliberately doesn't. Click one and press the combination you want.

These are the same everywhere, including in the profiles below: Windows hands a registered combination to one application system-wide, so a key this claims here is claimed in every application, and one set per application would need the registration to follow whatever is in front, which it doesn't.
hotkeys.sayWhenHidden: Show a message for a background capture while the overlay is hidden
hotkeys.sayWhenHiddenHelp:
A background capture puts a message on screen for a moment, so a hotkey that shows you nothing still tells you it worked. The overlay comes up for as long as that message lasts, drawing nothing else and passing every click straight through, then goes away again.

Off: a background capture leaves no trace at all until you next open the overlay.

This is only about the hidden case. With the overlay already up, in either mode, the message is always shown - it costs a frame that was being drawn anyway.
hotkeys.comboPrompt: Press a key... (click again to cancel)
hotkeys.comboTooltip: Click, then press the key combo you want - modifiers optional
hotkeys.comboRejected: Couldn't set that hotkey - it is already taken by another app
hotkeys.comboSetHere: Set here. Click to go back to the default (%s)
hotkeys.shortcutsHelp:
Keys that pick a tool, start something new, move snippets through the clipboard, or open the cheat sheet, while the overlay is up in edit mode.

Click a row, then press the key you want, or the middle or a side mouse button; Escape leaves it unbound. A key can only belong to one row, so taking it from another row is what happens if you reuse it.
hotkeys.shortcutPrompt: Press a key or button... (Esc clears)
hotkeys.shortcutTooltip: Click, then press the key or mouse button you want - or Escape to leave it unbound
hotkeys.shortcutSetHere: Set here. Click to go back to the default binding (%s)
_profiles: Settings > Profiles, and the target picker shared with the other tabs.
profiles.showingSettingsHelp:
Which settings are on screen: the defaults, the profile matching what the overlay is up over, or any other one.

A profile only states the settings it wants to change and takes the rest from the defaults, so the rows below are a mix. The ones this target states for itself are marked in accent and carry a revert arrow that hands them back to the default.

Editing a profile that isn't the one running is allowed - it just doesn't change anything until the overlay comes up over an application it matches.
profiles.showingShortcutsHelp:
Which shortcuts are on screen: the defaults, the profile matching what the overlay is up over, or any other one.

A profile only states the keys it wants to change and takes the rest from the defaults, so the rows below are a mix. The ones this target states for itself are marked in accent and carry a revert arrow that hands them back to the default.

Editing a profile that isn't the one running is allowed - it just doesn't change anything until the overlay comes up over an application it matches.
profiles.help:
A profile changes the Behavior settings and the Shortcuts while the overlay is up over one particular application. One applies at a time - the first in this list whose rules match - and everything it doesn't state for itself comes from the defaults.

A profile with no applications listed matches nothing and so never applies. That is a profile waiting to be finished, not a kind of profile.

A change to which applications a profile matches takes effect the next time the overlay is opened - the match is made on the way up, once, rather than followed while you work.
profiles.nothingToMake: Nothing identifiable to make a profile for.
profiles.makeForThisTooltip: Matched on the executable name, which is the half that doesn't change
profiles.newProfileTooltip: For an application that isn't in front of you - open it and name what it matches
profiles.name: Name
profiles.nameTaken: Another profile is already called "%s". This one keeps its name until you type one that is free.
profiles.nothingToMatchOn: Nothing to match on, so this profile never applies.
